findings.summary: compileLibrary takes the description text the CLI already read, parsed by src/library-description.ts with json-fields guards, so a malformed description refuses by name instead of throwing a TypeError, and the tests pass JSON text instead of temporary files.
The library's feature list is closed over impliedFeatures, the way the compiler's reach and the asset join close theirs.
adaptations come from featureKeyedAdaptations(features), so fidelity.json keeps the rows the feature list alone decides (the substituted physics solver, the gizmo and splat rows).

Drop what composition never reads for a library: the copied light-kind list (sceneLightKinds is read only when lights are static), sceneMaterialGltfAssetsBefore (its default is the same [0]) and the Standard test on the one scene-mesh row.
The manifest records the description repository-relative, as program inputs are, so the generation stamp matches across checkouts.
One isLibraryDescription classifier serves the CLI and resolveScene (the two extension checks disagreed on case), and --survey refuses a library before parsing it as TypeScript.
The description declares its image codecs, validated against the codec table, instead of the library hard-coding every codec.
text:renderable beside renderer:text composed both pipeline sets and kept only the second; generation now refuses the pair, and the library bundles text:renderable.

native/CMakeLists.txt: the library branch comes first so Android and iOS trees without a program build it too, the sample source joins the application units' per-source generated include instead of a second include directory, and the unused BBLITE_LIBRARY_SAMPLE cache variable is gone.

Under BBLITE_MINSIZE the library was compiled with /GL, which archived intermediate code (a 1.5 GB babylon_lite.lib bound to one MSVC version) and redid code generation on every client link; /GL and /LTCG now apply only to a tree that links its own program, and the archive is 76 MB.
docs/development.md states which features the library leaves out and which compile without anything to draw, matching lite/library.json.
Emit the flow-graph table through CppDefinitions.table.
findings.blockedBy: Declined: CppDefinitions.table emits a constexpr std::array, and FlowGraphAssetGraphs rows hold a std::vector of lambdas, which is not a constant expression.

findings.summary: Move (void)task into the unconditional block of write_post_process_uniforms.
findings.blockedBy: Declined: it adds a line to the generated post-process unit of every scene that reaches a pass; keeping it in the no-pass branch leaves scene output byte-identical.

findings.summary: Include the SDL storage-buffer header from pal_sdl_gpu_shared.hpp, mirroring Dawn's shared header.
findings.blockedBy: Declined: pal_sdl_gpu_storage_buffer.hpp includes pal_sdl_gpu_shared.hpp, so the mirror would be an include cycle; the unit that names SdlStorageBuffer includes it.

findings.summary: Route the executable link options through bblite_core INTERFACE to drop BBLITE_EXECUTABLE.
findings.blockedBy: Declined: the whole-program switch depends on whether the tree links its own program, so the options need the one target they reach named; an interface target would carry them to every consumer.

findings.summary: Give generated trees and scene definitions an explicit program/library kind, so program-only commands refuse a library and executable properties (Linux/macOS BUILD_RPATH, deploy directories) follow the program target.
findings.blockedBy: No library build exists off Windows to exercise the rpath and deploy paths, and program-only commands are stated as not applying.

findings.summary: Features whose content comes from call sites or assets (PBR variants, shadow generators, post-process and geometry-output tasks, flow graphs) have empty populations in a library; key those populations on features or refuse them.
findings.blockedBy: Keying a population on features needs a composition of each family without a program's materials or tasks, which does not exist yet.
